We could copy to archive folder by cd into archive and then cp from ../project_summary.txt? But cp cannot use paths. So we need to use mv? Actually we can use mv to move file to archive and rename. But mv also cannot use paths. So we need to cd into documents, then mv project_summary.txt to archive/summary_2024.txt? But mv cannot use paths. So we need to cd into documents, then mv project_summary.txt to summary_2024.txt? That would rename within same folder. Not good.

We might need to use cp to copy to archive folder by first cd into archive, then cp from ../project_summary.txt? But cp cannot use paths. So we cannot refer to ../. So maybe we need to use cp to copy to archive folder by first cd into archive, then cp from project_summary.txt? But the file is not in archive. So cp fails.

Thus we need to use cp with source: project_summary.txt, destination: summary_2024.txt, but we need to be in documents folder. Then we need to move the copied file into archive folder. But moving across directories is not possible. So maybe we can use cp to copy to archive folder by specifying destination: archive/summary_2024.txt? But cp cannot use paths. So maybe we can use cp to copy to archive folder by first cd into archive, then cp from ../project_summary.txt? But cp cannot use paths. So we cannot.

Thus we need to use cp to copy to archive folder by first cd into archive, then cp from project_summary.txt? But the file is not there. So we cannot.

Thus we need to use cp to copy to archive folder by first cd into documents, then cp to summary_2024.txt, then use mv to move to archive? But mv cannot use paths. So we cannot.

Thus we cannot copy across directories. But maybe we can use cp to copy to archive folder by first cd into archive, then cp from project_summary.txt? But cp cannot use paths. So we cannot.

Thus we cannot accomplish the request with the given tools. We should explain that.')
